title: Raster
description: A song title set in letters drawn only from horizontal and vertical strokes with 45-degree corners, and rendered only by the dot raster: a cell turns black when its centre falls inside a stroke, and nothing else is drawn. Drag up or down and the raster refines or coarsens, from five cells across a letter, a stair-stepped bitmap, to twenty, a fine screen. At every step the word breaks up into the dot field and each cell fades back on its own spring as the strokes sweep across it, so the word rebuilds itself from the grid. Type to change the title.
intent: After Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet (1967), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Alphabet, and his Vormgevers poster grid: accept the raster completely and let the letterforms come from it. Own glyphs, not the font.
